about.title: Sources and how it works
about.heading: Sources and how it works
about.intro: Where the numbers come from, how the score is made, where artificial intelligence is used and where it is not, and what this portal does not do.

score.heading: How the score is made
score.text: The score is computed by program code from public data, and the code is tested. For each measure, a district gets 0 to 100 points for how it compares with the other districts of the city (100 is best). The score is the weighted mean of those points. The weights are yours: on the page Find a district, or a preset.
score.limit: A score says how a district compares with the other districts of the same city. It does not compare cities, and it is not a grade of how good a place is to live.

ai.heading: Where artificial intelligence is used
ai.reports: The area report of each district is written by a language model from a fixed list of facts, ahead of time. Every report carries a label saying so.
ai.summary: The summary on the page Find a district is written by a language model when you ask for it, from the ranking on screen and your text. Your text is sent to an outside provider of the model and is not stored by us.
ai.translation: Stored text is translated between Polish and English by a language model before it is published. Nothing is translated while you use the portal.
ai.noScore: The score and the ranking are never computed by a model.
ai.noNumbers: A model never adds, changes or invents a number. A text that holds a number that is not in the facts is thrown away.
ai.noVerdict: A model never says that a district is safe or dangerous.
ai.guard: If a text cannot be written, the portal says so and everything else keeps working.

not.heading: What this portal does not do
not.listings: It is not a listings site. It shows no flats for sale or rent, no brokers and no links to offers. Rents are district medians.
not.safety: It makes no judgement of safety. Crime would be shown as recorded crimes per 10 000 residents, and Kraków has no crime data in this portal today.
not.forecast: It makes no forecast of prices. It shows history and a range seen in the past.
not.advice: It does not give financial or legal advice, and it does not ask who lives in a district.

sources.heading: Sources
sources.intro: Every source in use, with the credit line the licence asks for, as the data service gives it.

gaps.heading: Gaps in the data
gaps.intro: These figures have no data for this city. They are left out of the score. The reason is the data service's own text.
gaps.none: Every figure has data for this city.

a11y.heading: Accessibility statement (draft)
a11y.draft: This is a draft written during the HackYeah event. The city that hosts the service must complete and review it each year.
a11y.target: The target is the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2, level AA. The portal is not yet fully checked against it.
a11y.doneAuto: Every page is checked by an automated accessibility test in both languages.
a11y.doneContrast: Every pair of colours is tested for contrast: 4.5 to 1 for text and 3 to 1 for the parts of a control.
a11y.doneKeyboard: The pages have a skip link and a visible focus, and they fit a screen 320 pixels wide without sideways scrolling.
a11y.todo: What has not been done yet
a11y.todoScreenReader: A full check with a screen reader on each page.
a11y.todoZoom: A full check at 400 percent zoom on each page.
a11y.todoMap: On the two darkest classes of the map, the thin outline of a district does not reach 3 to 1 against its fill. Every district is also in the table next to the map.
a11y.reportText: The city that hosts the service will give a contact for accessibility problems. During the event, report a problem to the project team, or as an issue in the project repository on GitHub.
a11y.todoKeyboard: A full check with the keyboard alone on each page.
